questions.question: How can alcohol affect you while driving?

options.text: It makes it hard to think clearly.

questions.explanation: Alcohol weakens the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. You may feel overly confident or silly. Alcohol also slows your reaction time, hurts your coordination and balance, and makes it harder to judge distance and react to what is around you.

questions.question: Which of these substances can impair your driving and lead to a DUII arrest?
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving. These include all types of alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medications (both prescription and over-the-counter).

questions.question: If you are in a serious crash, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle and move it off the road if possible. If anyone is hurt, call 911 and help if you can. You must report crashes to police if there are injuries, deaths, or more than $1,000 in property damage (or more than $200 damage to government property like signs).

questions.question: How must license plates be displayed?

options.text: Attached securely so they don't swing.

questions.explanation: License plates must be fastened horizontally at least 12 inches from the ground so they don't swing. They must be clean and easy to read at all times.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Look over your shoulder at your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving your vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is true?

options.text: Never put an infant in the front seat of a car with airbags.
Airbags can hurt an infant or small child, even in a minor crash.
All passengers should wear a seat belt or use a child restraint.

questions.explanation: Always wear your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce your chance of injury or death in a crash. Children age 12 and under must sit in the back seat properly restrained. Never place a rear-facing infant car seat in the front seat if there is a passenger airbag.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what should you do?

options.text: Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show they are wrong.
Do something aggressive back to them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and get out of their way. Trying to get back at an aggressive driver makes the situation worse and more dangerous.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash?

options.text: Stay in the right lane on highways.
Drive only between 3 p.m. and 6 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single best thing you can do to reduce your risk of death or injury while driving.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Take turns more slowly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast on slippery roads is especially dangerous in turns and curves. Slow down more than you normally would when turning on wet or icy roads.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and let trains pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead. Slow down when you see it. Trains cannot stop for cars, so you must wait for the train to pass before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving?

options.text: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain activity and reduces your driving skills. It slows your reaction time and damages your judgment.

questions.question: You had an upsetting incident at work. When you reach your car, what should you do?

options.text: Play loud music so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the highway to release your anger.
Calm down for a few minutes before you drive home.
Stop at a bar and have drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down for a few minutes before you drive home.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, calm down before you drive. Driving while emotional is poor judgment and puts you and others at risk.

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing and see no train. When must you stop?

options.text: If a stop sign is posted.
If a crossing gate is down.

questions.explanation: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks if you see flashing red lights, a lowered crossing gate, a stop sign, a person flagging you to stop, or a train that is close. When in doubt, stop. Never try to race a train.

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When a flagger tells you to stop.
When a stop sign is present.
When flashing red signals and gates are operating.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing if a flagger tells you to, if there is a stop sign, or if flashing red signals and gates are operating.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off, what should you do?

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Flash your high beams at the driver.

questions.explanation: Do not take it personally when another driver cuts you off. Let it go and continue driving safely. This helps prevent road rage.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Stare at the driver as he or she passes.
Speed up as he or she passes.

questions.explanation: Move out of the way of an aggressive driver. Avoid eye contact. Do not speed up or block their way, as this may make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: What is true about drivers who drink alcohol before driving?

options.text: They are always aware of the risks.
They cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
They are better drivers because they are more careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol hurts your judgment, vision, focus, and reaction time. Never drink before driving.

questions.question: Why should you not follow other cars too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car ahead slows or stops suddenly.
You may not see the turn signals.
You may not see the brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car ahead slows or stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely and the car in front stops suddenly, you may not have time to avoid hitting it.

questions.question: When is it important to slow down?

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, near curves, around pedestrians, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: Where is passing not allowed?
questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills, curves, at intersections, or at railroad crossings. These areas are unsafe for passing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic flows in both directions ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow light?

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep going because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Watch what the other cars are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means red is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights, safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop. In heavy traffic, move slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: When should you signal when turning or changing lanes?

options.text: Always, even if no other cars are visible.
Only if there are other cars nearby.
Only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always, even if no other cars are visible.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb. Make this a habit, even when no other cars are present.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down, stay alert, and be ready to stop.
